chunks: And with this chain, from Safwan, from Khidhr, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Whoever gets angry, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will cover his head with a turban of fire.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of anger according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Thawab al-A'mal, Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) to highlight the spiritual gravity of uncontrolled anger, portraying it as a cause for divine humiliation. The 'turban of fire' (imamah min nar) serves as a specific eschatological mark of retribution, symbolizing how the head, often associated with dignity and leadership, becomes a vessel of punishment for those dominated by wrath. This imagery underscores the Shia emphasis on self-restraint (hilm) as a key virtue for attaining spiritual elevation and avoiding the ignominy of the Hereafter.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 3. And from the previous chain from Safwan from Khidhr from Muhammad b. Muslim from Abi Abdillah (a.s.) who said: “
The head of a bigot will be covered with fire by Allah.”
